title: Query tiling and tenant-tiered TTL 'Scorch' cache coordinator for low-tail dashboard latency
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Dashboard queries that request long time-ranges and many metrics are producing high tail latency for medium and large tenants. Current cursor-based pagination coupled with on-demand aggregation causes unpredictable fanout and repeated expensive scans. This ticket designs and implements a "query tiling" approach (split by time x metric tiles), a composite pagination protocol that merges partially materialized tiles, and a tenant-tiered TTL caching layer (internally named 'Scorch') combining tiny in-memory LRU shards and probabilistic bloom gating to reduce read amplification while preserving per-tenant isolation.
telemetry_requirements: trace span for tile fetch + merge per request
progress_updates: 2025-03-01: Kickoff meeting with Console Backend, Runtime, and Observability. Agreed on tiling axis (time, metric, granularity) and eviction heuristics for Scorch.
2025-03-02: Prototype of tile key encoding and deterministic merge order implemented. Initial microbench shows 25% reduction in median latency for synthetic 90-day queries.
2025-03-04: Integration spike with KV cache shim completed; discovered race between async rollup writes and tile eviction — added sequence numbers to tile metadata.
2025-03-05: Observability hooks added to prototype; dashboards for tile-level latency and cache hit-rate created in Grafana.
Next: implement tenant-tier admission control and speculative adjacent-tile prefetch for hot queries.
blockers: Finalize eviction policy for tenant-tiered LRU vs. TTL buckets (perf vs. fairness tradeoff)
Align runtime kernel for small tiled aggregation to avoid CPU blowup under high fanout
acceptance_criteria: 99th percentile end-to-end dashboard query latency reduced by >= 30% for affected workloads in staging
Pagination tokens remain stable across partial materialization and merges
Per-tenant cache isolation prevents noisy-neighbor eviction across tiers
Telemetry surfaces per-tenant tile metrics and end-to-end traces
rollout_plan: Start with opt-in flag for 10% of heavy-usage tenants in staging -> measure latencies and cache hit rates -> increase to 30% in canary region -> full rollout with migrate tool to convert existing paginated cursors to composite tiles. Fallback: route queries to legacy path if tile-merge latency exceeds SLA.
testing_plan: Unit tests for tile key encoding and deterministic merge algorithm
Load test with synthetic tenant mix (S, M, L) to validate fanout bounds
Chaos test: simultaneous rollup job and eviction to validate sequence number guard
End-to-end QA using real customer anonymized query traces
notes: Naming: 'Scorch' chosen to emphasize aggressive short-ttl tiering for hot slices; can be renamed in final docs.
We will coordinate with SRE for rollout throttles and autoscaling policies for increased CPU from merging work.
